keyVerseText: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,
rootMeaning: The root of אָגוּר (ʼÂgûwr) is אָגַר (ʼâgar), which means 'to gather' or 'to harvest.' The etymology as a passive participle suggests the meaning 'gathered,' implying one who has been collected or received among a group. This root sense enriches the understanding of the name Agur as not just a proper name but as someone who is 'gathered' or 'collected,' possibly among the wise or sages, indicating a status of inclusion and reception.
usageInScripture: The word אָגוּר occurs only once in Scripture, specifically in Proverbs 30:1, where it is used as a proper name, 'Agur, the son of Jakeh.' The top translation reflects this as 'of Agur,' underscoring its function as a personal name rather than a common noun. This singular usage highlights its uniqueness and identifies Agur as an author or compiler of proverbs, contributing a distinct voice to the biblical wisdom literature.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אָגוּר as 'gathered' enriches our appreciation of biblical authorship and wisdom. Agur, as one who is 'gathered,' symbolizes the faithful reception of divine truth and wisdom within the community of God's people. This name reminds believers that wisdom is not isolated but received and preserved through God's providential gathering of His servants. In Christ, the ultimate gathering of wisdom and revelation is fulfilled, as He embodies the perfect revelation of God's truth, gathering His people into one body through His word.
keyVerseReflection: Proverbs 30:1 introduces 'The words of Agur the son of Jakeh,' identifying the source of this prophetic wisdom. The name Agur, meaning 'gathered,' adds depth to this introduction, suggesting that the teachings come from one who is received among the wise. This verse sets the tone for the unique and inspired insights that follow, emphasizing the divine gathering of wisdom that Agur represents.
